issues.claim: Smith.ai AI-first entry, contract_terms: "10% discount for a 12-month term; 30-day money-back guarantee (refund of plan and add-ons up to $1,000, overage excluded) stated on the human-first page"
issues.problem: These terms are not on smith.ai/pricing/ai-receptionist, which I re-opened. That page's own contract answer says the AI Receptionist is month-to-month, 'there aren't any long-term contracts', and that cancellation requires 30 days' notice, and it offers a 6-month plan for a lower per-call rate rather than a 10% 12-month discount. The money-back guarantee and the 10% 12-month discount appear only on smith.ai/pricing/receptionists. Putting them in the AI-first entry's contract_terms presents human-first terms as AI-first terms, and the cancellation mechanics differ.
issues.fix: Move the 10%/12-month discount and the 30-day money-back guarantee out of the AI-first entry (leave them only in the human-first entry). For AI-first, state: 'Month-to-month, no long-term contract, 30 days' notice to cancel; 6-month plan offered for a lower per-call rate (rate not published).' Keep the caveat that the two structures are separate.

issues.claim: price_ranges.full_service_or_custom: "separately $2.75/call at the top of the published per-call model (ServiceTitan AI Virtual Agent)"
issues.problem: Contradicted by the brief's own sourced data. ServiceTitan's page says 'usage-based, starting at $2.75 per call' — that is the floor of its range, not the top of per-call pricing generally. Smith.ai's human-first plans work out far higher per call ($300/30 = $10.00, $810/90 = $9.00, overage $11.50 on Starter), and Smith.ai AI-first Pro is $2.00/call with a $3.00 overage on Free. A reader would take away the opposite of what the sources show.
issues.fix: Reword to: '$2.75/call is ServiceTitan's published starting per-call rate; per-call pricing in this set runs far higher at Smith.ai (about $9-$10 per call on human-first plans, $11.50 overage on the 30-call plan).' If the point is that it is the only vendor-published per-call rate on an AI agent, say that instead.

issues.claim: one_line: "live human answering sits between at $159-$2,100/month"
issues.problem: Unit/billing-term slip. SIAS bills $159 per 4-week cycle with 13 cycles a year — its page states '$159 every 4 weeks is about $172 per calendar month' — so $159 is not a monthly price. The offerings entry gets this right; the summary sentence does not, and the summary sentence is what gets reused.
issues.fix: Change to 'live human answering runs $172-$2,100 per calendar month ($159 per 4-week cycle at SIAS, $2,100 for Smith.ai human-first Pro)', or add '(~$172/calendar month)' after $159.

issues.claim: buyer_reported_costs, Reprise AI case study: "A Tampa HVAC contractor reportedly paid $1,400/month ... year: 2026"
issues.problem: The $1,400/month figure and the 'bilingual answering service' context are on the page and check out, but the page carries no date and contains no occurrence of '2026' (nor any year), so the stated year is unsupported. Check 3 requires the year to come from the source.
issues.fix: Set year to 'not stated on page' for that entry (as the two Reddit entries already do), or date it only if a published/updated date can be found.

issues.claim: one_line low band "self-serve AI at $49-$150/month" versus price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve "$29-$150/month"
issues.problem: Internal inconsistency: the summary excludes the $29 Jobber AI Receptionist add-on that the range text uses as its floor, and the range text also pulls Goodcall Starter/Frontdesk in at $79-$99 while Goodcall's own $129/$299 self-serve tiers sit in the mid band. The band boundaries can be read two ways.
issues.fix: Use one figure in both places ($29-$150, flagged that the $29 is a third-party-sourced add-on), and add one clause saying Goodcall's $129/$299 self-serve tiers are counted in the mid band because they include job booking and multi-tool integration, not because of price.

issues.claim: price_ranges.mid_market top anchor: "90 calls (Smith.ai human-first Basic $810)" inside a band described as "trades-focused AI CSR or hybrid human/AI desk"
issues.problem: The price is correct, but Smith.ai's human-first Basic is a live-human receptionist plan, which the brief puts in a separate 'live human answering' band in the one_line. Using it as the top anchor of the AI/hybrid band mixes the two categories, so the $810 ceiling is a human-service price rather than an AI-CSR price.
issues.fix: Either relabel the band as 'trades-focused AI CSR or hybrid desk, plus live-human comparator' or cap the AI/hybrid band at the highest AI/hybrid anchor (Sameday Scale $789 / Abby Professional $599 / Smith.ai AI-first Enterprise $500) and show $810 only as the human-service comparator.
